RadioOptionGroup (src/components/ui/form: Container: accessibilityRole="radiogroup"; optional testID prop applied to that same container.

Each row: accessibilityRole="radio" + accessibilityState={{ checked }}; accessible name (accessibilityLabel) is the option's `label` string ONLY -- a `sublabel`, if present, is a separate visible Text node, not merged into the accessibilityLabel (qa-lead assumption #1, flagged for batch review).
Row press calls onChange(option.value) unconditionally, every tap, including re-tapping the already-checked row (matches Select.tsx's onValueChange precedent) -- never suppressed as a no-op.
onChange must not fire merely from rendering/mounting.
option.label and option.sublabel (when given) are both rendered as visible text, queryable via getByText.
RadioConfirmModal (src/components/ui/cor: visible=false renders none of: title text, any radio row, Confirm text, Cancel text (matches plain RN Modal + the pre-existing DuplicateSlotChoiceSheet/RemoveStepModal convention).

visible=true renders title, optional body, one RadioOptionGroup built from `options`, and a fixed two-button footer with the LITERAL strings "Cancel" then "Confirm" (queried via getByText -- no accessibilityLabel contract imposed, qa-lead assumption #2).
Internal `selected` state seeds from defaultValue and MUST reset to defaultValue every time `visible` transitions false->true (a selection made before closing must not survive reopen).
Tapping a radio row only moves `selected` locally -- must never call onConfirm or onCancel by itself.
Confirm calls onConfirm(selected) using whatever is currently selected (including an untouched defaultValue).
Cancel calls onCancel and must never call onConfirm, regardless of whether the selection was changed first.
DuplicateSlotChoiceSheet (FE-3): External props unchanged: visible, slotLabel, existingProduct, incomingProduct, onReplace, onKeepBoth, onCancel.
Radio options exactly: {value:'replace', label:'Replace'} (defaultValue), {value:'keep_both', label:'Keep both'} -- queried via getByRole('radio', {name:'Replace'|'Keep both'}).
Confirm dispatches to onReplace when selection is 'replace' (incl. the untouched-default case), onKeepBoth when 'keep_both'. Cancel calls onCancel only.
RemoveStepModal (FE-4): External props unchanged: visible, productName, dow, onRemoveDay, onRemoveAll, onCancel.

Radio options exactly: {value:'day', label:`${dayPlural} only`} (defaultValue -- narrower/less-destructive, NOT a previously-primary button since none existed here), {value:'all', label:'All days'} -- e.g. dow=1 -> 'Mondays only' radio name, dow=5 -> 'Fridays only'.
Confirm dispatches to onRemoveDay for 'day' (incl. untouched default), onRemoveAll for 'all'. Cancel calls onCancel only.
DraftPreviewScreen bottom commit-scope f: onCommit(scope: PlanCommitScope) signature unchanged; onClose unchanged.
Radio options exactly: {value:'both', label:'Morning & Evening'} (defaultValue), {value:'am', label:'Morning Only'}, {value:'pm', label:'Evening Only'} -- queried via getByRole('radio', {name: ...}).
Confirm calls onCommit(selected) (incl. untouched 'both' default). Cancel calls onClose and must never call onCommit (same behavior as the old 'Cancel / Discard Draft').
Per tech design, this footer uses RadioOptionGroup directly + a local Confirm/Cancel Button pair -- no new Modal/BottomSheetModal nesting.
The per-step 'Change' affordance and the cycle-class-rival prompt card (Alternate automatically / Keep just this one) are UNRELATED, untouched by this task -- do not convert them.

deviations_and_findings_for_batch_review: RadioOptionGroup's outer container needed an explicit `accessible` prop in addition to accessibilityRole="radiogroup" for RNTL's getByRole('radiogroup') to find it -- isAccessibilityElement() only returns true when `accessible` is explicit or the host type is Text/TextInput/Switch, so a bare accessibilityRole alone is not enough. The pre-existing PhototypeStep.tsx radiogroup (no `accessible` prop) was never actually queried by role before this task, so this is a previously-latent gap in the house convention, not a new one introduced here.

RadioConfirmModal's `body` prop renders inside a Text (not a View) -- forced by qa-lead's fixture passing a bare string (`body: <>Choose which periods to update.</>`), since RN requires bare text to be a child of Text, not View. DuplicateSlotChoiceSheet's multi-line body (nested Text nodes) still works because Text-inside-Text is valid RN, but a future caller wanting layout-bearing body content (e.g. icon + text row) would need a follow-up change to this prop's rendering.

Fixed a regression in tests/routine-similar-product-priority/add-to-routine-sheet-duplicate-flow.test.tsx, an AddToRoutineSheet-level integration suite NOT in qa-lead's files_modified list, which also exercised the old getByLabelText('Replace <name>')/'Keep both'/'Cancel' select-and-commit-in-one-tap assertions at 6 call sites. Rewritten to the same select-radio-then-getByText('Confirm'/'Cancel') pattern qa-lead already established in the sibling duplicate-slot-choice-sheet.test.tsx file -- a mechanical fix to the fixed contract, not a new interpretation of it. Flagged per standing instruction to surface any discrepancy for batch review.

findings_verdicts.finding: 2. RadioConfirmModal's `body` prop renders inside a Text, not a View.

DuplicateSlotChoiceSheet's multi-Text body still renders correctly (Text-inside-Text is valid RN, confirmed via passing tests). Type-B technical gap, already documented in the engineer's progress-log entry, satisfying architecture-review.md section 6's bar for downgrading a deviation. Diffed the file directly: a 1:1 mechanical substitution (getByLabelText('Replace <name>'|'Keep both'|'Cancel') -> getByRole('radio', {name}) + getByText('Confirm'|'Cancel')) at all 6 call sites, identical in shape to qa-lead's own rewrite of the sibling duplicate-slot-choice-sheet.test.tsx file. findings_verdicts.finding: 4. DraftPreviewScreen's commitScope resets to 'both' on visible->false.
findings_verdicts.reasoning: Traced the real caller (src/screens/RoutinesScreen.tsx): visible={draft !== null}, and every in-session update path that keeps the draft open (handleSwapAlternative, handleOverride/handleAcceptCycleSplit) replaces draft directly from one non-null object to another non-null object in a single setState call -- draft never passes through null mid-session, so visible never flips false except on genuine close. The engineer's own hypothetical risk does not occur on the real wiring. Matches RadioConfirmModal's own reset-on-reopen convention. No blocker.
